correctness.rationale: An injective word has distinct deletion faces and a Boolean interval of subwords, so its ordered simplex gives the regular cellular model with signed deletion. Independently generated the group using x↦x+1 and x↦−1/x, both determinant-one projective transformations; their closure has 60 elements, the full group since |SL₂(F₅)|=(25−1)·5 and the scalar kernel has order 2. With the stated reference order the signed matrices give cell counts (6,30,120,360,300,60) and differential ranks (5,25,95,235,60) in degrees 1–5. Independent integral reduction had only unit invariant factors in each matrix, so the integral homology has no torsion: torsion of H_d is torsion of coker(∂_{d+1}) since im(∂_d) is free. The resulting reduced groups are Z³⁰ in degree 3 and Z⁵ in degree 4 only. Full word counts through length four give the full three-skeleton of the six-letter injective-word complex. That complex is a wedge of five-spheres, and cellular approximation gives the two-connectivity of its three-skeleton and therefore of the present complex. Purity follows from generation by full-length words; nonzero homology below dimension five rules out pure shellability.
residual_risks: This checks the specified reference order and action, not all six-point actions or all choices of reference order. Algebraic cancellation does not classify the full homotopy type.

value.rationale: A canonical small nonabelian projective group action is a meaningful test for the topology of subgroup-generated word complexes. A full low skeleton and integral homology in two different intermediate degrees distinguish it from full-word and pure-shellable models. The exact ranks and torsion exclusion provide a reproducible benchmark for other natural group actions without assuming a larger classification.
residual_risks: No general-field theorem, higher homotopy classification, or automorphism representation is established.
